title: West Pakistan Highways Sindh Amendment Act 1973

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Highways Sindh Amendment Act 1973
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

ACT II OF 1973
ACT II OF 1973
WEST PAKISTAN
HIGHWAYS (SIND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
An Act to amend
the West Pakistan Highways Ordinance, 1959
In its application
to the Province of Sind
[Gazette of Sind,
Extraordinary, Part IV, 29th June 1973]
(First published after having
received the assent of the Governor of Sind in the Gazette of Sind
(Extraordinary), dated 28th June 1973).
No. PAS/Legis-B.1/73.-The
West Pakistan Highways (Sind Amendment) Bill, 1973 having been passed by the
Provincial Assembly of Sind on the 4th June 1973 and assented to by the
Governor of Sind on the 8th June 1973 is hereby published as an Act of the
Legislature of Sind :-
1. Short title and
commencement.---(1) This Act may be called the West Pakistan Highways (Sind
Amendment) Act, 1973.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.

West Pakistan Ordinance XXXII of 1959.---In the, West Pakistan Highways

"(dd)

and Hyderabad via Bahram Goth from mile 8 to mile 97:"

Insertion of section 22-A in West Pakistan Ordinance XXXII of 1959

ACT II OF 1973
ACT II OF 1973

An Act to amend
the West Pakistan Highways Ordinance, 1959
In its application
to the Province of Sind
[Gazette of Sind,
Extraordinary, Part IV, 29th June 1973]
(First published after having
received the assent of the Governor of Sind in the Gazette of Sind
(Extraordinary), dated 28th June 1973).
No. PAS/Legis-B.1/73.-The
West Pakistan Highways (Sind Amendment) Bill, 1973 having been passed by the
Provincial Assembly of Sind on the 4th June 1973 and assented to by the
Governor of Sind on the 8th June 1973 is hereby published as an Act of the
Legislature of Sind :-
4. Insertion of section 22-A
in West Pakistan Ordinance XXXII of 1959.---In the said Ordinance, after
section 22, the following new section shall be inserted :
"22-A. Ban
on commission of certain acts.-No person shall commit any act (including
discharge of water from the lands under cultivation or any other source and
draining of diesel coil, mobile oil or other lubricating oils from vehicles)
within the highway that damages or is likely to cause damage to the road, its
sub-grade, surface, term or any of its structures, or which causes or is likely
to cause obstruction to the traffic on the highway, and no person shall, except
under permission of the Highway Authority, damage or cut the trees along or
within the limits of the highway. "

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Highways Sindh Amendment Act 1973
sections.description:
Substitution of section 24 of West Pakistan Ordinance XXXII of 1959

ACT II OF 1973
ACT II OF 1973
WEST PAKISTAN
HIGHWAYS (SIND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
An Act to amend
the West Pakistan Highways Ordinance, 1959
In its application
to the Province of Sind
[Gazette of Sind,
Extraordinary, Part IV, 29th June 1973]
(First published after having
received the assent of the Governor of Sind in the Gazette of Sind
(Extraordinary), dated 28th June 1973).
No. PAS/Legis-B.1/73.-The
West Pakistan Highways (Sind Amendment) Bill, 1973 having been passed by the
Provincial Assembly of Sind on the 4th June 1973 and assented to by the
Governor of Sind on the 8th June 1973 is hereby published as an Act of the
Legislature of Sind :-
5. Substitution of section 24
of West Pakistan Ordinance XXXII of 1959.---In the said Ordinance, for
section 24 the following section shall be substituted :
"24. Constitution
of Mobile Courts and cognizance, and trial of offences.- (1) Government
may constitute Mobile Courts of Special Magistrates having jurisdiction over a
particular highway or part thereof, and cognizance, of any offence under this
Ordinance or rules made thereunder shall only be taken by such Court either suo
motu or on complaints made to it.
(2) Except where the Mobile Court
deems it desirable that an offence be tried otherwise all offences under this
Ordinance or the rule made thereunder shall be tried summarily.
(3) For the purposes of
preventing offences under this Ordinance and trying them on the spot the Mobile
Court may as often as it deems fit patrol the highway under its
jurisdiction."
